# Groovy JVM provider and release evidence

This is the evidence ledger for the planned `jvm` product. Groovy is the product
name; Groovy language support is a separate release decision. An upstream
manifest or download link establishes an available integration, not a passed
Groovy workflow or permission to redistribute its binary.

## Historical import-policy checkpoint — 2026-10-16

Maven `ignored_pom_patterns` persist through the existing settings owner (7.70).
The bounded internal contract passes local model and Copper Rust regression
checks (7.71). Development provider `0.30.0` retains the advertised
`groovy.maven.importReactorWithMasks` command in the existing M2E import handler
(7.72). Its cached, network-denied headless fixture passes fresh and restarted
reactors, individual POM masks, exact directory exclusions, required-library
replacement, masked parents with active children, empty selections, cancellation
and changed-input recovery. Direct production checks cover the pinned matcher
language, portable path admission, Unicode and bounded matching work. Old Maven
requests and phase-only receipts remain compatible. The cached Reader also
retains imported child models when an aggregate/root has no cached model
(7.75). Exact 0.29.0 controls lose one/five models; 0.30.0 preserves them in
fresh/restarted fixtures. Unavailable identities and incomplete coverage remain
explicit. Reads use existing cached facades and never discover/import projects. Existing Gradle metadata
compatibility passes 60 checks after its fixture selects IPv4 localhost through
the existing denied-network client and scoped CLI environment. External network
denial and production Gradle behavior are unchanged. This fixture restriction
does not qualify the application’s default dual-stack IPC under its actual
network-permission policy; that remains part of the host settings and native gates.

Saved masks with explicit selected roots now use the existing local LSP phase
owner only when the current provider advertises the qualified v2 command (7.73).
Current imported/ignored POM facts survive read refresh and dependency-graph
collection with settings, visibility and imported-membership admission. Obsolete
classifications are dropped while current permitted data remains partial; no
required/orphan classification or full synchronization is inferred. Mask-only
default-root policy remains 7.3, shared-tree editing remains 8.7 and remote phase
facts remain 7.76. These bounded software checks do not establish native controls,
remote execution, physical Windows behavior, full tool-window parity, complete
synchronization or provider redistribution rights. `jvm` remains planned. See [M05 in the parity inventory](./groovy-tool-window-parity.md#capability-matrix)
and the [canonical plan](../../../.agents/specs/groovy-jvm-product/tasks.md).

README](https://github.com/Kotlin/kotlin-lsp/blob/d266c18c3e7791ea1ac5bf49a3ab77a33c0be465/README.md)
still identifies alpha and partly closed implementation.

workflow or resource verdict. The macOS ARM64/32 GiB reference and 8 GiB combined
editor/JVM/build-worker RSS ceiling remain unchanged. No new binary, adapter,

review. Historical entries below retain their exact original inputs.

The Java extension [requires JDK 21 or newer for managed JDTLS](https://github.com/zed-extensions/java/blob/5c4b7650d5d949ab3cbc4f84ffe1539d474609bd/README.md). Its Gradle server can use a separately configured JDK, and the project target runtime may differ from both. The extension's optional JDK auto-download is not a Groovy first-run action without explicit user approval. The Java and Kotlin extensions' source licenses do not establish licenses for fetched JDTLS, Kotlin LSP, Lombok, Gradle or Debug binaries.

The installed macOS ARM64 Kotlin server identified itself as `ILS-263.4702.0`;
its `product-info.json` has build number `263.4702.0`. Its extracted
`license/third-party-libraries.json` lists 168 components under 17 license
labels, alongside other license files. This is an inventory of the downloaded
candidate, not a review of every component or a grant to redistribute the
partially closed-source server. The [official release list](https://github.com/Kotlin/kotlin-lsp/blob/main/RELEASES.md)
still headed `263.4702.0` on 2026-09-30 and describes its links as weekly
pre-alpha builds. Groovy still needs a fixed binary selection, complete
license/notice review, and platform checks before a package claim.

The [current official release list](https://github.com/Kotlin/kotlin-lsp/blob/main/RELEASES.md)
publishes separate VS Code extension and standalone-server artifacts. Its
earlier release notes say the VS Code extension uses the
[JetBrains Free Plugin License](https://www.jetbrains.com/legal/docs/terms/jetbrains-free-plugin-license/)
instead of Apache 2.0; that agreement restricts transfer of the covered plugin
without express permission. The release list does not say this VS Code license
governs the standalone archive that the Zed Kotlin extension downloads. A
review of the installed `263.4702.0` macOS ARM64 standalone archive found
third-party license inventories but no top-level license naming rights to
redistribute that complete archive. Neither the source repository's Apache 2.0
file nor the VS Code extension's license resolves the standalone binary's
terms. Groovy may continue evaluating extension-managed downloads, but a
bundled or mirrored Kotlin server remains unapproved pending an authoritative
standalone license and redistribution decision.

The reviewed Java extension's [`languages/java/tasks.json`](https://github.com/zed-extensions/java/blob/5c4b7650d5d949ab3cbc4f84ffe1539d474609bd/languages/java/tasks.json) uses `/bin/sh` for its
run and test tasks. Its [README](https://github.com/zed-extensions/java/blob/5c4b7650d5d949ab3cbc4f84ffe1539d474609bd/README.md#launch-scripts-aka-tasks-in-windows) says those launch scripts work out of the box on
macOS and Linux, while Windows requires custom task scripts. Windows build and
selected-test behavior therefore cannot be claimed from extension installation
alone. The reviewed Kotlin extension resolves the latest official server from
the mutable `main/RELEASES.md` on an uncached launch; its [README](https://github.com/zed-extensions/kotlin/blob/d457cf46cc74ed0f455f746d4c411d135ace5408/README.md) also documents
an explicit local binary override. A Groovy release candidate needs a frozen
binary and checksum or a separately reviewed update policy before its alpha
server can count as verified.

A standalone LSP probe opened the checked-in two-module Maven fixture with the
alternate server. It returned `Kotlin Language Server 1.3.13`, a `Greeting`
document symbol, hover text, and an empty diagnostic publication for a valid
file. Those shallow responses did not establish a healthy project import. The
server logged `Unable to find the 'mvn' command or suitable wrapper` for module
POMs, although it found the root `mvnw`: its pinned resolver looks only beside
each POM for a wrapper when `mvn` is absent from `PATH`. A disposable root
`mvn` executable made that lookup succeed, yet the server then reported no
Maven artifacts and a `KotlinFrontEndException` with
`NoDescriptorForDeclarationException` while analyzing `Greeting`. The same
root wrapper's exact `dependency:list` command completed successfully outside
the server after the disposable fixture and cache were primed. This candidate
fallback is **blocked for the multi-module Maven cell**; empty diagnostics and
local symbols must not be shown as successful fallback evidence. Completion,
definition, restart, installed-extension launch, remote behavior and other
physical platforms remain untested for that Maven cell. The product must keep
fallback selection deliberate and show provider failure rather than
automatically claiming that this alternate makes the official alpha server
release-ready.

The same pinned alternate on a disposable copy of the two-module Gradle
fixture found the root wrapper and logged successful dependency and build
script classpath resolution. A stronger standalone Gradle probe then resolved
`Greeting` from a second Kotlin file, offered `message()` completion, pushed
one `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE` error for an invalid edit, and cleared diagnostics
after the source was restored. Its isolated Gradle daemon stopped and the
disposable fixture was removed. One earlier attempt had the same semantic
responses but raced fixture cleanup while a shared Gradle daemon was still
writing; the isolated rerun removed that harness ambiguity. This is a **partial
Gradle fallback candidate**, not a supported release cell. A repeatable probe
of the re-downloaded `1.3.13` asset matched the locally recorded SHA-256, then
passed two launches on the same disposable Gradle fixture with a JDK 17: the
first logged dependency and build-script resolution, and both resolved
`Greeting`, completed `message()`, published one error for an invalid edit,
and cleared it after restoration. The first took 42.1 seconds and the warm
restart 5.3 seconds. A second two-launch run changed only the disposable root
wrapper to invoke Gradle with `--offline` before the restart; the same semantic
checks passed in 39.5 and 5.2 seconds, and the fallback again logged Gradle
resolution. A guarded repeat took 42.6 and 5.5 seconds and recorded nine
invocations of that offline wrapper during the restart, so the server did
actually use the modified wrapper. Its `semantic-ready` probe label is based
on these observations;
the alternate server did not report JetBrains' terminal import status. This
proves one cached wrapper-offline restart, not OS-level network denial. The
installed extension, remote host, other platforms, empty-cache failure,
and bundled dependency terms remain unverified. The Maven failure still
blocks a general fallback claim.

An additional macOS ARM64 probe ran that same pinned alternate under a
process-local `(deny network*)` sandbox. Its first Gradle launch answered
cross-file definition, document symbol, and completion requests, but did not
publish the initial clean diagnostics before the probe's 40-second deadline;
the command exited nonzero before restart. This broad sandbox can also restrict
local Gradle communication, so the timeout does not establish a server defect.
At that point it left OS-denied-network fallback behavior unverified; the
cached restart below provides a narrower positive result.

A narrower macOS Seatbelt profile now permits localhost TCP and binds while
denying other network access. A disposable empty-directory HTTP server returned
`200` through this profile on `127.0.0.1`; external DNS and a direct external
TCP attempt failed. A cold first launch with this profile answered cross-file
definition, symbol, and completion requests, but did not reach clean
diagnostics at either 40 or 120 seconds. Retained LSP notifications showed
`MISSING_BUILT_IN_DECLARATION` for `kotlin.String`, and the server log said it
could not resolve the Kotlin standard library from the empty isolated Gradle
cache. The first launch was an incomplete-cache failure, not an absence of
diagnostic publication or proof of a server defect.

The corrected cached-offline probe first warmed that same isolated state with
network available, then restarted pinned fallback `1.3.13` with its Gradle
wrapper forced offline and the narrower Seatbelt profile active. The two
launches took 69.4 and 8.3 seconds. On the denied-network restart, the probe
recorded nine offline-wrapper invocations, cross-file definition to
`Greeting.kt`, `message()` completion, one invalid-edit error and empty
diagnostics after restoration. The direct child peak resident sample reached
680,132,608 bytes across both launches. The reviewed archive hash above
identifies the distribution; the extracted launcher in this run had SHA-256
`29543a848c2027b7058acc20f7fa6c8f53e8bd2aba49856eb7cd17608f7427cc`.
This establishes one standalone cached Gradle fallback under process-local
non-local network denial on macOS ARM64. Cold cache, installed extension,
remote host, Maven fallback, complete process-tree resources and other
platforms remain open.

On 2026-09-30 the same pinned fallback passed the two-module Gradle fixture
with 100 added Kotlin sources on two normal launches (44.0/8.3 seconds). The
probe checked a symbol, definition to `Greeting.kt`, and clean diagnostics in
the last added file, plus completion and invalid-edit/recovery diagnostics in
the original probe. A separate warm-then-restart run with the Gradle wrapper
forced offline and non-local network denied passed the same checks
(41.5/10.9 seconds); the denied restart invoked the offline wrapper nine times.

was JDTLS `1.61.0`. The

`338e7e73d61836651ba2453919a0d34fa763eb4e7c03342092309bffb8934c64`.

disposable two-module Maven and Gradle fixtures imported. `getAll` returned

The connected fake-host fixture now holds a Kotlin export across replacement

A later retained-handle variant exposed a shared UI invalidation gap: removal

The repeatable standalone check is
`python3 script/test-groovy-jdtls-provider.py --jdtls /path/to/jdtls/bin/jdtls --java-home /path/to/jdk-21-or-newer`.
It copies the repository's Maven and Gradle fixtures into disposable worktrees,
checks both module roots, expected source paths, project VMs, and the Gradle
project dependency, then requests definition navigation into a generated Java
file. It requires a separately acquired JDTLS archive, a compatible JDK and
locally cached fixture dependencies. It does not exercise the product's
extension or remote-host path.

The `jvm-tools` candidate adds Maven and Gradle build Tasks when a project root
contains a matching wrapper and build file. Its source selects Unix scripts or
Windows batch wrappers from the host worktree path style. A local fake-worktree
test passed wrapper detection, task-root resolution and hiding a private Maven
wrapper while retaining the Gradle action. The JVM-feature workspace Task test
passed for denial before an untrusted build spawns, success after a trust
transition, denial of the same saved Task after its wrapper becomes private,
and stale-build denial after worktree removal. The production TerminalPanel
has run a disposable wrapper-shaped script through a trusted generated Maven
Task, including a nonzero exit. The checked-in Maven and Gradle fixtures have
each run a selected test through their wrappers from the shell on macOS ARM64,
including an offline rerun from a populated cache. Opt-in fixtures now copy
both projects into fresh worktrees and run each generated build Task through
the production TerminalPanel; both completed and wrote JUnit reports with a
host JDK and populated caches on macOS ARM64. A third product Task fixture
forces Maven offline with an empty repository: the Task fails, its terminal
shows the missing plugin problem, and no JUnit report is created. OS-level
network coverage is bounded: on macOS ARM64, both cached fixture
build Tasks passed through the production TerminalPanel in fresh worktrees and
wrote JUnit reports while a Seatbelt profile denied outbound TCP ports 80 and 443. A direct TCP 443 probe succeeded outside that profile and failed inside
it. The profile kept local sockets available for Gradle. Under a stronger
`deny network*` profile, Maven still passed, but Gradle failed before building
because its file-lock contention service could not create a local socket;
that result does not test Gradle dependency resolution. The success checks do
not establish behavior for all network protocols, an empty Gradle cache,
remote execution, or a packaged Groovy build.
Windows Task, a Java test with a real child process launched from the Tests
view, and remote-host build remain unverified workflow cells.
The planned flavor's Windows x64 onboarding fixture did pass on a native
`windows-2022` runner at
[`9a69a297a1`](https://github.com/simtropolis/made/actions/runs/36389684750/job/108822544107).
It checked `.exe`, `.cmd`, and `.bat` lookup, same-installation `java` and

incompatibility. It did not open Groovy or install a toolchain.

The `jvm-tools` candidate can parse bounded completed JUnit XML from
[Maven Surefire](https://maven.apache.org/surefire/maven-surefire-report-plugin/)
and [Gradle `Test` tasks](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/java_testing.html)
into the existing structured result types. The parser requires a module
manifest path for permission filtering, rejects malformed or oversized XML,
and withholds selected-test actions unless a separate provider has verified
the exact case-to-method mapping. [JUnit display names](https://docs.junit.org/6.0.3/api/org.junit.jupiter.api/org/junit/jupiter/api/DisplayName.html)
and [parameterized names](https://docs.junit.org/6.2.0/writing-tests/parameterized-classes-and-tests.html)
need not identify an invocable method. Parser tests alone do not prove a live
JUnit Jupiter run or native Tests action behavior.
The reviewed Java extension's [runnable query](https://github.com/zed-extensions/java/blob/5c4b7650d5d949ab3cbc4f84ffe1539d474609bd/languages/java/runnables.scm)

requires an exact JUnit `@Test` capture and conventional module test-source
path matching the report case before it can provide a selected-test identity.

and display names do not. A local producer now verifies saved Java test source
against these captures before offering a selector; its focused fixture uses a
Java-named grammar and query, not an installed Java extension.
The host-side collector reads only `TEST-*.xml` under the selected Maven or
Gradle module, caps individual and aggregate report size and file count, and
uses the worktree-confined file reader. Fake-host tests consumed both checked-in
reports and rejected an out-of-worktree report symlink. The selected action
captures a confined report version before Task scheduling, then collects again
after terminal completion. Only a changed report containing that exact case
publishes a current result; an unchanged report yields an unverified diagnostic
and no passing case. The shared confined reader now has a Windows candidate
that checks opened file IDs, rejects reparse endpoints and verifies normalized
final paths against the opened worktree root. Its ordinary read, replacement,
root replacement, and parent-junction assertions passed on native Windows x64
at [`f35466e3ce`](https://github.com/simtropolis/made/actions/runs/36355491934/job/108722350690).
The JVM provider also collected an ordinary Maven report and rejected a
parent-junction escape through `RealFs` on native Windows x64 at
[`67c6a23696`](https://github.com/simtropolis/made/actions/runs/36386432630/job/108812674775).
Native Maven/Gradle child-process execution, remote-host, and packaged workflow
checks remain required before that release cell passes.

The pinned Java extension's own selected-test scripts use `/bin/sh`; they do

rejection, and no false pass from unchanged XML. An opt-in macOS ARM64 fixture

access to its existing host cache for a lock file. A separate local Unix
fixture starts a real child through the same Tests and terminal path, cancels
from Tests, then releases the test-controlled child wait and verifies a
Cancelled structured run with no late completion.
A connected physical remote run, packaged-app cancellation, and Windows
behavior remain unverified. Maven Surefire method filtering passed in the

With an empty Maven repository and forced `-o`, a selected Tests-panel action

The downloaded macOS ARM64 proxy and bridge archives matched their published
size and SHA-256. Each contained only its named executable, with an ARM64
Mach-O header and no license or notice file. They were inspected without
executing or installing them in this review. This establishes two archive
identities and six listed platform cells, not execution on those platforms,
a complete notice set, a reproducible-build attestation, or approval to bundle.
The pinned extension source's Apache-2.0 license does not complete a transitive
binary review.

The same extension's
[`gradle_ls.rs`](https://github.com/zed-extensions/java/blob/5c4b7650d5d949ab3cbc4f84ffe1539d474609bd/src/gradle_ls.rs)
fixes its library source to publisher `vscjava`, extension `vscode-gradle`,
version `3.18.0`; it extracts `extension/lib/` from the publisher's
[VSIX artifact](https://vscjava.gallery.vsassets.io/_apis/public/gallery/publisher/vscjava/extension/vscode-gradle/3.18.0/assetbyname/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Services.VSIXPackage).
The downloaded 33,124,107-byte archive had local SHA-256
`c9b31e8c824447d1c7561d73fad6b382f4345086bc78aa0905bec938b5352a9c`.
No independent publisher digest was checked for this VSIX. Its package
manifest confirms that publisher and version, references Microsoft's
`vscode-gradle` repository, and names `LICENSE.md` as its license.
The archive's top-level MIT license is 1,071 bytes with SHA-256
`5cab8f71748fb317bee6f1794b8eb02dbe3021aedbf264eb8fd453ad6748eebe`;
`NOTICE.txt` is 188,174 bytes with SHA-256
`42653457ffd4d5e23171bbb2534eadb7ca7e048406e0673bc927ed813db02ff2`.

There are 36 JARs under the extracted `extension/lib/`, including
`gradle-tooling-api-9.2.0.jar`, the Gradle server, bridge-facing API and
language-server libraries. Their complete artifact-to-notice mapping remains
unreviewed. For example, the notice lists Gson `2.9.0` while the archive names
`gson-2.9.1.jar`; that difference is a review input, not a finding of a license
violation. The top-level MIT terms and recorded notice file do not settle
all transitive redistribution obligations. This archive review did not
install or run the VSIX.

The Gradle bridge's provider contract projects plugins, closures and build
script classpaths into the Gradle language server. It does not expose an
effective Maven/Gradle build or test JDK to Groovy. Its per-server
`lsp.gradle-language-server.settings.java_home` override is distinct from
`lsp.jdtls.settings.java_home`; neither setting selects Task compiler/test
JDKs. The guide now states that limit instead of implying automatic JDK-role
resolution. Task 1.1, JDK-role acceptance under 2.1/flavor 7.3, and the release
cell gates remain open.

that Maven interoperation is impossible with a future provider version.

recommends `<extensions>true</extensions>` on the Kotlin Maven plugin for mixed
Java and Kotlin sources. A disposable copy of this fixture replaced its manual
Kotlin compile execution with that extension mode, pinned Maven resources and

compiled `Greeting.class`, but the same standalone JDTLS `1.61.0` import
removed it and Java definition still returned no target. This rules out the
fixture's manual Kotlin plugin execution as the sole cause of this candidate

## Required evidence before a cell is supported

1. Freeze extension revisions and every managed server and adapter version.
   Record registry provenance, archive URLs, SHA-256 values, transitive notices,
   permissions and binary redistribution terms. If redistribution is not
   allowed, use the existing explicit on-demand download flow and state the
   network requirement.
2. Run a cached multi-module Maven and Gradle fixture with generated sources,
   Java and Kotlin diagnostics, completion, navigation, host JDK resolution,
   dependency import, build, selected JUnit test, stable test identity,
   cancellation and one supported Java DAP breakpoint. Capture process and
   source paths, exact archive hashes and logs.
3. Run incomplete-cache, denied-network, untrusted worktree, missing/wrong JDK,
   failed download, alpha-server crash/restart, user-selected Kotlin fallback,
   remote disconnect and permission-revocation variants. Show actionable UI
   errors and no stale result or hidden retry.
4. Verify a native package's identity, launcher and update namespace and a
   keyboard plus real screen-reader journey on each advertised desktop target.
   Automated source checks may establish IDs, settings precedence, fixture
   results and package metadata; native launch, debugging, host process
   location and spoken accessibility require physical platform evidence.

## Cached official Kotlin Gradle import with external downloads denied

On 2026-09-30 the earlier official Gradle daemon-listen probe failure was

also failed the loopback filter; explicit IPv4 networking fixes that probe-only
mismatch. Sharing the existing cache then encountered an active cache-journal
lock, so the successful fixture clones wrapper/caches into a new Gradle user home
and daemon registry for each launch. Only copied lock files are removed. The
original host cache and its existing daemon are preserved.

`script/test-groovy-kotlin-provider.py --cached-denied-network` is a macOS-only
successful-import mode for the official Gradle server with an explicit build JDK.
It retains failed disposable state for diagnosis. It permits local TCP/UDP and
bind/listen, with external outbound traffic denied. A disposable Gradle init
script attempts external TCP from the actual import JVM and requires `Operation
not permitted`, rather than accepting a timeout or refusal as denial. The probe
matches that PID to its isolated Gradle 8.13 registry and uses `lsof` to require
only loopback TCP listeners. Gradle can detach from the server's process session,
so cleanup uses the isolated launcher's `--stop --gradle-user-home` and requires
all daemon PIDs recorded in that registry to disappear before returning success.

## Maven Kotlin navigation after provider refresh

On 2026-09-30, a disposable copy of the checked-in mixed Maven fixture was
imported by the same standalone JDTLS `1.61.0.202609031315` candidate on JBR
`25.0.4.1`. The probe enabled the existing Kotlin-support option and disabled
JDTLS autobuild only in that disposable experiment. Maven used the cached
wrapper, offline mode and an explicit Zulu JDK `17.0.19+10-LTS`; the server's
reported project VM was a separate JBR 17 installation. No product default,
project classpath, fixture manifest or provider binary was changed.

After import, `mvnw -o -q -DskipTests package` succeeded and produced
`library/target/classes/evidence/Greeting.class`. Sending the existing
`workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles` class-change notification did not restore
Java definition navigation to `Greeting.kt` during the 45-second poll.
The probe then sent JDTLS's documented
`java/projectConfigurationsUpdate` notification for both module POMs,
requeried the two-module/source-root model, rebuilt offline and sent the class
watch notification again. The subsequent 45-second definition poll also
returned no target while the Kotlin class remained present. Both module source
and target levels were 17; Maven dependency-attribute checks still passed.
The configuration notification is asynchronous: the five-second wait and model
requery are not an independently observed refresh-completion acknowledgement.
This negative probe rules out these tested sequences, not every Maven provider
configuration or a future upstream fix.

Pinned upstream source was inspected at tag `v1.61.0`, commit
`08eafe6ff60c7159ef88571d47b6a9ef82fef94e`:

- [Gradle Kotlin init script](https://github.com/eclipse-jdtls/eclipse.jdt.ls/blob/08eafe6ff60c7159ef88571d47b6a9ef82fef94e/org.eclipse.jdt.ls.core/gradle/kotlin/init.gradle)
  adds compiled Kotlin output directories as exported binary classpath entries.
  The Gradle importer selects it when Kotlin support is enabled. No equivalent
  Maven Kotlin hook was found in the reviewed manager/handler source; that is a
  source-search result, not a claim about every transitive Maven configurator.
- [SearchUtils](https://github.com/eclipse-jdtls/eclipse.jdt.ls/blob/08eafe6ff60c7159ef88571d47b6a9ef82fef94e/org.eclipse.jdt.ls.core/src/org/eclipse/jdt/ls/core/internal/SearchUtils.java)
  looks up other-language source from a binary Java member and its class-file
  metadata. A class existing on disk alone does not establish that member in
  JDTLS's Java model. The output-entry difference is a plausible explanation
  for the passing Gradle and failing Maven samples, not a proven complete cause.
- [ProjectConfigurationUpdateHandler](https://github.com/eclipse-jdtls/eclipse.jdt.ls/blob/08eafe6ff60c7159ef88571d47b6a9ef82fef94e/org.eclipse.jdt.ls.core/src/org/eclipse/jdt/ls/core/internal/handlers/ProjectConfigurationUpdateHandler.java)
  forces provider configuration updates through the existing project manager.
  `java.project.updateClassPaths` instead rewrites the provider's raw classpath;
  it was not used to fabricate a passing Maven model.

Source base: `e556c376705102acbf61db25541f2fa5c6779fd9`. Disposable probe SHA-256:
`704c1d884b954be5457dfb906d871a4c0411bb7e2e562424f41b3f6124ac4ca3`.
Captured log SHA-256:
`6bdf66f0fdacf1baddcd2cd01917a20b9bd391efe249806b4309065949776b8d`.
The experiment catches each navigation assertion to report both negative

## Installed fallback acquisition and host failure recovery — 2026-10-01

Source checkpoint: `62cc8e309ce92dd42536f3a1a61534fa3f82271e` plus the
three changed Rust files, whose combined Git diff SHA-256 is
`2d254168c6786138a95fa6989a696428f8c0feef6159c253ab6b948e907f2bc5`.
The source changes belong to existing Groovy tasks 1.2 and 1.4. Neither task
nor a release gate is marked complete.

### Installed Kotlin fallback cannot bypass download policy

The existing opt-in installed-WASM fixture now invokes `kotlin-language-server`
from registry Kotlin extension 0.3.2/API 0.5.0, alongside its preferred
`kotlin-lsp` path. The reviewed pinned [fallback implementation](https://github.com/zed-extensions/kotlin/blob/v0.3.2/src/language_servers/kotlin_language_server.rs)
asks for GitHub release metadata and then `server.zip`. Fake metadata supplies
version 1.3.13 and that archive URL. With empty host capabilities, the actual
compiled extension returns `download_file` / `not granted by the extension host`
before the artifact URL reaches FakeHttpClient or a launch command is returned.
The fixture asserts the exact metadata request sequence: official Kotlin release
notes, fallback GitHub releases, and Lombok tags for the cached Java proxy stage.
No Kotlin cache artifact is created, and Java/Kotlin defaults remain enabled
without an extension-install failure entry.

Artifacts and proxy are the same SHA-256-identified installed inputs recorded in
the two preceding sections; no upstream archive, platform or license claim is
added. The fallback is directly invoked by the fixture. This does not prove
normal settings selection, automatic bootstrap, fallback semantics, OS-wide
HTTP denial, process-capability denial or a packaged Groovy application.

`GROOVY_JAVA_PROXY` inputs with offline Cargo, debug information disabled and two
build jobs:

```sh
  -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
```

### Existing LSP status owner supplies bounded recovery

Installed-WASM acquisition exposed a remaining presentation gap: the shared
startup status forwarded the host download-capability error without a bounded
JVM recovery action. The existing Project helper now recognizes only the
observed download-denial signature for `jdtls`, `kotlin-lsp` and

that helper before publishing failed binary acquisition to LanguageRegistry,
covering errors reported before a server process exists. No status service,
permission policy, installer, server selector or provider registry is added.

The message names the project host, permission review or an installed server
binary, and restart. Kotlin messages preserve server choice and state that the
fallback needs its own permission or installed binary. Private URLs, query
tokens and stderr paths are absent from that status; the original startup reason
remains in the existing host log. Non-download failures, Rust Analyzer and
builds without `jvm-tools` keep existing behavior. The change grants no new
capability and launches no fallback automatically.

The local delegate integration exercises the actual Project/worktree delegate
and shared binary-status stream, including Copper's unchanged Rust status.
Unit cases cover error and stderr signatures, private details, unrelated
network/process errors and ordinary startup stderr. These are source and
host-delegate checks, not changed-source native presentation, remote status
transport, successful retry or fallback import. The prior alternate Maven
semantic failure remains blocked.

## Cached Java process permission and recovery status — 2026-10-01

The existing opt-in installed-WASM fixture now isolates the stage after cached
Java setup acquisition. It still proves denied cold proxy, both Kotlin archive
paths and cached-proxy Lombok downloads. A fresh pinned Java 6.8.27 instance then
uses a disposable copy of complete installed JDTLS 1.61.0 and actual Lombok
1.18.48 with the explicit provider override
`lsp.jdtls.settings.check_updates = "never"`. The existing WasmHost capability
granter denies `process:exec /usr/bin/java ["-version"]` before execution and
before a launch command. Neither the native proxy nor Java, Lombok or JDTLS is
executed. The exact three permitted fake metadata URLs remain unchanged across
the whole fixture. Enabled defaults and the extension-install failure ledger
stay unchanged. This is cached override and host-capability evidence, not normal
update behavior, OS-wide HTTP denial, a fresh acquisition success, catalog
bootstrap or product installation.

The cache input is explicit `GROOVY_JAVA_CACHE`; the existing
`GROOVY_INSTALLED_EXTENSIONS` and `GROOVY_JAVA_PROXY` inputs retain the versions
and hashes recorded above. The copied JDTLS directory contains 223 files totaling
69,633,132 bytes. Actual `lombok-1.18.48.jar` is 2,055,065 bytes with SHA-256
`85477a4655ebb2c074a9099cfb749be454449fee564d4282610df1b85f7c508b`.
It is not renamed to the earlier fake Lombok 1.18.42 metadata version: the
explicit never-update cached phase makes no Lombok request. The retained input
manifest `/private/tmp/groovy-cached-java-process-inputs.json` lists every copied
JDTLS relative filename, size and digest plus Lombok; its SHA-256 is
`08ec191dc2ed1828ee725c5ef8e98e6eb4325159dd5546eefcdc88ae8776f78f`.
These installed-cache facts do not independently approve provenance or terms.

The pinned [Java provider's configuration source](https://github.com/zed-extensions/java/blob/5c4b7650d5d949ab3cbc4f84ffe1539d474609bd/src/config.rs)
(SHA-256 `63767129e5d998e1c461d0add2828f41f75a4964cb9ccdf19f85d8d4faafba87`)
confirms the explicit `never` behavior; its default is `always`. Its
[JDTLS launch builder](https://github.com/zed-extensions/java/blob/5c4b7650d5d949ab3cbc4f84ffe1539d474609bd/src/jdtls.rs)
and [Java version utility](https://github.com/zed-extensions/java/blob/5c4b7650d5d949ab3cbc4f84ffe1539d474609bd/src/util.rs)
locate the observed probe after resolving JDTLS and before constructing the
returned command. Their inspected SHA-256s are
`e5d3275593c34cd41c750127d517cf230fc6000ba1ee11f9de99398d2054b649`
and `6a0b65fe2839cf0852821e392a4a3c167186c751ddccea6d1a2df043a39d4eba`.
The existing shared WASM process owner calls `grant_exec` before spawning. No
permissions are granted or policy bypass added.

### Existing status owner correction

`jdtls_startup_error` now recognizes only the observed Java-version setup prefix,
host process-denial signature and exact `-version` argument. Its static recovery
message asks for extension process permission review on the project host and
restart, and explains that cached server files do not imply process permission.
Host filenames and stderr paths are omitted. The original error remains in the
normal startup log. Generic process denials, other arguments, other servers and
JVM-feature-off builds retain their previous status behavior. Preferred/alternate
Kotlin selection and host capabilities do not change.

The real local `LocalLspAdapterDelegate`/LanguageRegistry fixture now checks both
download and Java-probe denial for all three JVM IDs and Rust Analyzer. With
`jvm-tools`, only the observed JDTLS probe is mapped; Kotlin's unrelated process
error stays raw. With JVM tooling absent, every status stays raw, protecting
Copper's shared owner. There is no new process manager, permission registry,
status store, provider selector or UI framework. This remains tasks 1.2 and 1.4;
both are partial. The development guide and design describe the bounded behavior.

```sh
GROOVY_INSTALLED_EXTENSIONS=/private/tmp/groovy-smoke.bh47ws/data/extensions/installed \
```

## Maven autobuild corroboration — 2026-10-01

At source revision `b13fde9e2ac4cf574ccef7c8e7440b98d3d0beb4`, a fresh disposable copy of the
canonical mixed Maven reactor was built with its cached wrapper using
`mvnw -o -q -DskipTests package`. Standalone JDTLS 1.61.0 used the complete
JBR 25 installation from the verified Kotlin standalone candidate. Both its
initialization options and later configuration supplied the existing experimental
Kotlin support option and `java.autobuild.enabled=false`. This is a repeated
negative configuration, corroborating the earlier provider-refresh experiment;
no product defaults, classpath, provider binaries or canonical fixture changed.

The compiled `library/target/classes/evidence/Greeting.class` existed before
import, after module discovery and after definition. Provider source-root
discovery returned the expected application and library modules, and the
application classpath exposed `evidence:library:1.0-SNAPSHOT` plus the Kotlin
stdlib, annotations and JUnit dependencies. Definition at `new Greeting()`
in `Main.java` still returned `[]`. This confirms that deleting the class is
not the sole observed failure condition in this candidate. It does not prove
that every Maven layout or future provider version fails.

The initial observer read only the live message queue, although the shared
probe retains notifications consumed by a request in a separate deque. The
corrected observer inspected both sources after definition, then drained the
queue for twelve seconds. Neither source yielded a diagnostic publication for
`Main.java` in that bounded window. Absence of a publication is not a clean
diagnostic report or proof of diagnostic availability. The probe exits normally
when it records a negative definition response; its exit code is not a passing
Java-to-Kotlin workflow gate.

## Gradle build-script server setup denial — 2026-10-01

The existing Java extension also owns `gradle-language-server` for Gradle
build scripts. Its immutable [Gradle launch builder](https://github.com/zed-extensions/java/blob/5c4b7650d5d949ab3cbc4f84ffe1539d474609bd/src/gradle_ls_server.rs)
acquires the [3.18.0 VSIX libraries](https://github.com/zed-extensions/java/blob/5c4b7650d5d949ab3cbc4f84ffe1539d474609bd/src/gradle_ls.rs)
before its bridge and Java command. The conventional `src/lib.rs` lookup was
absent; the pinned Cargo entry locates the actual `src/java.rs` dispatch. This
source review identifies the tested setup route, not a distribution right or
a new version claim. Gradle build-script support does not decide general
Groovy programming-language support.

`gradle-server.jar`. It verifies SHA-256/RSA-4096 signatures naming Microsoft
Corporation through the existing JDK truststore's DigiCert Trusted Root G4.
The recorded timestamp authority is DigiCert; UTC timestamps are
**2026-07-06 01:08:08** and **2026-07-06 11:46:50**, respectively. The logs
retain signer expiration **2027-10-30** and timestamp expiration **2031-11-09**.
Neither JAR is executed or modified. This is stronger than merely finding
`MSFTSIG` filenames; it is a bounded signature check against this local
truststore, without an explicit online revocation check. It does not authenticate
the entire VSIX, prove the unsigned custom JARs' publisher identity, attest the
source/build recipe, or grant redistribution rights.

Together with the preceding **31** exact primary third-party artifact matches,
all **36 top-level Gradle JARs** now have independent artifact identity or
controlled class-source evidence. Complete archive publisher-digest validation,
notice/version reconciliation (including JSR305), nested legal coverage,
redistribution/delivery rules and release-platform workflows remain open.
No distribution claim or Groovy-language support is added. Task 1.1 stays
partial; `jvm` stays planned with no targets. Native app action-time confirmation
remains pending and VoiceOver remains skipped.

## Installed Java cached command recovery and fresh-host revocation — 2026-10-01

The existing opt-in installed-WASM fixture now continues after its cached
Java process denial. It uses the same shared SettingsStore, WasmHost,
CapabilityGranter and WorktreeDelegate, with Java **6.8.27** and Kotlin
**0.3.2** still loaded from the installed manifests/WASM. No new permission,
process, setup or result owner is added, and no product code changes.

A complete disposable cache now also copies the installed Debug cache:
`com.microsoft.java.debug.plugin-0.53.2.jar`, **3,107,682 bytes**, SHA-256
`5275195905015ce786fc6318c8d039fef43a1fada1d03acdec24c69a3b9ba83c`,
plus its existing update marker. The copied JAR is neither executed nor
independently cleared for redistribution. Previous JDTLS/Lombok/proxy inputs
retain their hashes and scope recorded above. The explicit new
`GROOVY_JAVA_HOME` input selects the previously checksum-verified Temurin
**21.0.12.1+1** macOS ARM64 installation; its `bin/java` SHA-256 is
`9be1d0a740ff6502df1a762145e62860f5de4b7e17658d9cb9498da3acf9d16c`.
The test passes that path through `lsp.jdtls.settings.java_home`; the delegate
still advertises the competing `/usr` JAVA_HOME and `/usr/bin/java` PATH
candidate. Cache updates remain explicitly `never` for this fixture.

Two sequential fresh-host states verify:

1. A single grant allows only **that exact Java executable with `[-version]`**.
   Installed WASM runs its real version probe and returns the cached relative
   `bin/v6.8.27/java-lsp-proxy` command. The fixture checks the command exists
   inside the extension work directory, that its Java launch arguments select
   the explicit JDK, and that its returned `JAVA_HOME` agrees. The native proxy,
   JDTLS, Lombok and Debug adapter are not launched.
2. After removing that grant, a new host/extension instance denies the same
   explicit executable's version probe before returning a launch command.
   A cached command/provider does not grant a fresh host permission.

Both states make **zero additional HTTP requests** beyond the prior three
fake metadata URLs. Enabled Java/Kotlin defaults and their automatic-install
failure ledger remain unchanged. The original denied instance is dropped
before the transition. This is fresh-host settings/capability and cached-command
recovery evidence; it does not prove hot revocation of an existing WasmHost,
normal provider update behavior, fresh acquisition success, provider startup,
product/native error presentation, remote delivery or a platform/package pass.

### Failed fixture assumptions retained

- The first compile stopped because a PathBuf in an assertion diagnostic used
  Display without `.display()`; the test diagnostic was corrected.
- The first runtime recovery delegate omitted `HOME`. Pinned Java provider
  `expand_home_path` requires that variable even for an absolute override;
  it logged `Failed to expand ~`, ignored the configured JDK and reached the
  denied `/usr/bin/java` probe. This remains a provider contract limit for a
  host missing HOME, not a silently repaired upstream/product behavior. The
  corrected fixture supplies the ordinary HOME entry `/capability-fixture`;
  its absolute JDK override remains unchanged. No host/system environment is
  modified.
- The next run resolved the command but its fixture assertion expected a
  `java/` prefix. Actual WasmExtension returns the provider's relative `bin/`
  command; the existing launch owner resolves it against `work_dir`. The
  assertion now checks that real contract and its cached file. No path or
  launch implementation changes.

## JVM permission recovery names the authoritative host restart — 2026-10-01

The preceding fresh-host recovery exposed a setup action gap in tasks 1.2/1.4:
`WasmHost::new` captures `ExtensionSettings.granted_capabilities` when the shared
ExtensionStore creates it, and new WASM instances on that host receive the
same grant snapshot. Restarting a language server or reloading an extension
therefore does not apply a changed host grant. The prior download/probe messages
asked for a language-server restart without identifying this host lifetime.

The installed Java 6.8.27 fixture now retains its original denied host. After
an explicit compatible JDK override and exact `-version` grant are written to
SettingsStore, a freshly loaded Java extension on the **same** host still
returns the version-probe denial, naming the configured JDK. Its original
host grants remain empty. Only a **new** WasmHost resolves the cached relative
proxy command; removing the grant then denies another fresh host. All stages
retain exactly the prior three fake metadata URLs and unchanged product-default
and failure-ledger state. The existing Debug cache and checksum-verified
Temurin 21.0.12.1+1/macOS ARM64 inputs remain those recorded above. All four
prior WASM/Java-manifest/JDK-executable input hashes are rechecked and unchanged.
The proxy, JDTLS and Debug JAR are not launched. This adds real installed-WASM evidence
for the host lifetime without introducing hot permission changes or altering
the shared capability granter.

The existing Project LSP startup/binary-status helpers now ask for the
**application or remote server on the project host** to restart after changed
extension grants. The cached Java process-denial message also explains that
host grants are read at startup. Download-denial messages retain the alternative
of a compatible installed binary and a normal language-server restart. They
retain deliberate Kotlin selection and existing permission checks. Signature
matching is unchanged; static bounded copy continues to omit private artifact
URLs, query tokens and stderr/toolchain paths. Ordinary JDK setup failures,
non-JVM servers, unrelated process errors and JVM-feature-off builds retain
existing actions/status. Original error logging is unchanged.

Requirement 2.3, design and the development guide identify this authoritative
host restart. They do not imply that a client reconnect creates a new remote
extension host, add a remote restart command, change project trust, grant a
capability or certify physical permission recovery. The current source
correction is distinct from the earlier recorded installed-product statuses;
no older binary is credited with these new messages.

## JDTLS embedded legal inventory — 2026-10-01

Task **1.1** now has a recursive, read-only inventory of the already reviewed
Eclipse JDTLS `1.61.0-202609031315` archive. The retained archive remains
**51,037,522 bytes**, SHA-256
`338e7e73d61836651ba2453919a0d34fa763eb4e7c03342092309bffb8934c64`,
matching its retained Eclipse sidecar. No provider was launched, downloaded,
modified or bundled during this audit.

The archive contains **128 regular files**, including **115 top-level JARs**.
Seven JARs contain **78 nested JARs**, for **193 JARs** in the inspected tree.
Each JAR, recognized legal file and embedded Maven metadata file has a retained
SHA-256. The audit unfolds OSGi manifest continuation lines and records bundle
identity/version, vendor, `Bundle-License`, legal-file names and links,
embedded POM license declarations and parent coordinates. It rejects duplicate
ZIP names and oversized inputs, bounds recursion and aggregate JAR bytes, and
rejects POM DTD/entity declarations. It reads the original archive without
extracting or changing its contents.

| Observation                                        | Top-level JARs | Nested JARs | Total |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------: | ----------: | ----: |
| JARs inspected                                     |            115 |          78 |   193 |
| JARs with recognized embedded legal files          |             82 |          57 |   139 |
| JARs with `Bundle-License` declarations            |             37 |          18 |    55 |
| JARs with neither recognized files nor that header |             23 |          13 |    36 |
| Recognized legal files                             |            106 |         115 |   221 |

The file and header categories overlap. Recognition covers `about.html`,
`about_files/` contents and license/notice/copying/copyright/EPL filenames;
it is not a legal conclusion or proof that all terms appear under those names.
Sixteen JARs have explicit license declarations in embedded POMs. In particular,
nested `jcl-over-slf4j-1.7.36.jar` lacks a recognized legal file/header but
its POM declares Apache License 2.0. Absence from a file/header category does
not establish absence of a license.

### Concrete remaining mapping work

- The **23 top-level JARs** without recognized files or `Bundle-License`
  are **21 Flexmark 0.64.8 wrappers**, JetBrains annotations **24.0.1**, and
  IntelliJ Java decompiler engine **253.29346.240**. Their exact file hashes and

  The SLF4J POM declaration above is recorded. Parent-bundle legal files must

  every child inherits its container's license.
- Observed manifest declarations include EPL 2.0/LGPL 2.1, EPL 2.0/GPL
  Classpath links, EPL 1.0, Apache 2.0, BSD 2/3 clause and MIT links. These

  choices, modified/shaded payloads, copyright/notice completeness, corresponding
  source obligations, or Groovy's notice/source delivery.
- The archive has no recognized top-level legal file. Embedded legal files
  still need a component-to-terms/delivery review. The extension's dynamic

Task 1.1 remains **partial**. This inventory narrows the previous unreviewed
archive state and identifies exact missing mappings; it does not approve

### Modified Jansi boundary

Bundled `org.fusesource.jansi:jansi:2.4.3` is **275,077 bytes**, SHA-256
`d8a8fe4462c7916c95ebaf8708a98d24b13a1ab5d3514316ec1270d30ce20a73`.
The published JAR is **258,321 bytes**, SHA-256
`ec168cf31c4c3849348dfff7a04e90170615f7784f1255ee6747b98a854c04c5`.
No payload path is added or removed. Differences are:

- `META-INF/versions/9/module-info.class`: read-only `javap -v -p`
  shows that the bundled descriptor adds the `ModulePackages` attribute
  for its existing packages. The module's requirements/exports remain
  identical in the decoded output; this does not prove a source rebuild.
- `org/fusesource/jansi/internal/native/Mac/{arm64,x86,x86_64}/libjansi.jnilib`:
  `codesign --display --verbose=4` reports Eclipse Foundation Developer ID
  authority, team `JCDTMS22B4` and hardened-runtime flags on each bundled
  payload. The displayed timestamps are 22 May 2026 at 06:13:12/13 in the
  host's local display. The published ARM64 payload is linker/ad hoc signed;
  published x86/x86_64 are unsigned. An initial audit assertion that every
  published payload was unsigned failed on ARM64 and was corrected to retain
  the observed signature states.

This is signature **display**, not static signature verification, online
revocation/notarization checking, code-section equivalence, runtime validation
or authentication of the entire JDTLS archive. It identifies a concrete
modified/native provenance boundary that remains open. The POM's Apache 2.0
declaration is retained separately from those binary differences.

## Official Kotlin vendor components and SwingX identity — 2026-10-01

Task **1.1** follows the five exact Maven Central misses using the documented
JetBrains IntelliJ dependency repository. The repository discovery inputs are
retained at immutable observations of
[JetBrains' repository configuration](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/blob/517c4075b4811ab8dec0d7bf8ee8a4b59ee5e6cb/.idea/jarRepositories.xml)
and the [native-certificate project README](https://github.com/JetBrains/jvm-native-trusted-roots/blob/4f02855d8bf47db9a920b033da2af1d39f183189/README.md).
These commits establish where the publisher documents retrieval; they do not
identify the source revision used to build the candidate's components. No
provider classpath, package or runtime changes.

The report keeps both original declarations and the stale embedded snapshot
metadata. This resolves a bounded published-payload identity discrepancy;
it does not silently substitute a version or establish license/source delivery,

### Source and notice boundaries

Exact vendor source classifiers are available for Commons Imaging, Ini4j and
native certificates, retaining **405 Java source payload hashes**. Commons
Imaging has 343 sources: 342 carry an Apache 2.0 marker before their package,
and the placeholder TgaImageParser has the same commented text after its
package line. All 47 Ini4j sources carry the marker before their package.
None of the 15 native-certificate source prefixes carry that marker; the exact
POM declaration remains separate evidence. Absence of an individual marker
is not an unlicensed-component claim. Source classifiers alone are not an
immutable Git source pin or controlled source-to-class reproduction.

## Official Kotlin LZ4 macOS static verification — 2026-10-01

Task **1.1** narrows the two changed native resources in the exact
`at.yawk.lz4:lz4-java:1.11.0` comparison. The original Maven JAR and candidate
SDK wrapper are rehashed; the wrapper is also rebound to the retained official
Kotlin ZIP/.sit, whose publisher-matched SHA-256 remains
`95da3fc6d3b9092c7616345044a05edb85e5408dc648d081e4e433595c892bec`.
Extraction is limited to the four exact resource payloads. Neither library is
loaded, executed, installed or modified. The earlier bounded Jansi Mach-O parser
is reused by selecting its function definition, with its source digest retained;
none of its unrelated top-level commands run.

### Native payload and section observations

All **11 ARM64** and **10 x86-64** section records match their published

whole-file, source-build or runtime equivalence.

### Restricted and normal-host signature outcomes

Initial restricted `/usr/bin/codesign --verify --strict --verbose=2` checks
return exit 1 for both bundled libraries with “invalid signature”; signature
display reports unavailable authority. The same immutable files and commands
then run with normal host access and return **exit 0** for both bundled files,
with valid-on-disk/designated-requirement messages. Normal-host display identifies
`Developer ID Application: JetBrains s.r.o. (2ZEFAR8TH3)`, Apple certificate
chain and timestamps. These observations distinguish restricted failures from
normal-host static acceptance; no file is repaired, re-signed or replaced.

The original published ARM64 file has an ad hoc linker signature and passes

## Official Kotlin Velocity shading and XMLRPC filter mapping — 2026-10-01

This follow-up narrows two missing-path rows in task **1.1** using the retained
publisher-matched Kotlin `263.4702.0` macOS ARM64 archive. It adds no product,

published artifacts, source declarations and observed SDK payloads remain
separate evidence classes.

### Published payload and declared minimization

All **256 class payloads** and every common file in SDK
`lib/intellij.libraries.velocity.jar` match the exact Maven Central
`org.apache.velocity:velocity-engine-core:2.3` artifact. Whole JAR hashes differ;
the SDK adds its index/module descriptor and omits five legal files.

The published artifact already contains the shaded Commons IO classes
`FilenameUtils` and `IOCase`. Its exact POM declares Maven Shade **3.2.1**,
`commons-io:commons-io` inclusion, SLF4J exclusion, relocation from
`org.apache.commons.io` to `org.apache.velocity.shaded.commons.io`, and
`minimizeJar=true`. The published parent POM names tag `2.3-RC2`, resolved through
the primary Apache mirror to commit
`9cd6c031f9a2b36b6c922b9f86c3034b822e8870`. Its source parent POM is byte-identical
to the published parent; the source core POM differs from the reduced published
POM but retains the identical raw shading contract and Commons IO **2.8.0**

paths** in the candidate's Velocity wrapper. Original and shaded class hashes

## Combined cached Gradle Project/provider workflow — 2026-10-02

Task **6.1** now has an opt-in real-provider Project integration fixture,
`jvm_workflow::cached_gradle_project_keeps_both_jvm_providers_and_test_identity`.
The fixture reuses RealFs, the shared Project/LSP lifecycle and trust registry,
JVM provider snapshot reducers, JUnit discovery and structured identity, and
selected Task planning. Its Java grammar is a development dependency only.
Test adapters bind explicit cached server commands; they do not load installed
extension WASM, fake provider replies or exercise automatic extension bootstrap.
No product-code, second model/result store or panel framework is added.

### Observable assertions and prerequisites

The disposable source copy excludes prior `.gradle` and `build` directories and
asserts all three host/generated-output roots are absent before preparation.
The recorded source inventory binds the **15 tracked fixture files**, not the
ignored outputs of earlier runs. Explicit preparation executes the cached
Gradle **8.13**, Kotlin plugin **2.0.21**, JUnit Jupiter **5.11.4** two-module
`:application:build` with `--offline --no-daemon`; it checks newly generated
`BuildMessage.java` and compiled Kotlin `Greeting.class`.

The same Project opens Java and Kotlin sources and starts JDTLS **1.61.0** and
JetBrains official Kotlin LSP **263.4702.0**. Launchers, JDK release metadata,
fixture hashes and test source/binary are bound in the retained evidence.
Provider runtime is explicitly JBR **25.0.4.1+1-b583.48**; fixture build runtime
is Temurin **21.0.12.1+1**. These are controlled prerequisites, not a product JDK
resolver, silent installer or accepted release-version choice. The earlier
publisher-matched archive and governing-terms limitations remain unchanged.

Assertions require two distinct server IDs, current Java/Kotlin project
snapshots (observed **2 Java projects / 7 Kotlin projects**), provider dependency
facts, generated Java and Kotlin source roots, Java-to-Kotlin and generated-source
definitions, and a saved Kotlin method-call edit resolving to its declaration.
The Kotlin edit is restored and saved. Current source-backed JUnit discovery
keeps a stable case ID across generations; old-generation plans fail and fresh
plans pass. Revoking worktree trust removes both snapshots and the selected plan;
teardown waits for **both actual PIDs**, as well as cleared LSP handles.

Both final clean-copy variants pass on macOS ARM64: normal **16.98 seconds** and
external-network-denied **16.57 seconds**, one passing test each. Both
prove two provider PIDs stop. The denied variant reuses the existing

## Combined Project Java diagnostics and applied quick fix — 2026-10-02

The same task **6.1** real-provider fixture now adds Java language checks through
existing Project/LSP and Buffer APIs. Its disposable `LanguageProbe.java` is
created only in the temporary fixture. Project completion includes `println`.
An unsaved missing-method edit produces an error overlapping that call and
naming `missingMessage`. Project requests enabled quick fixes and applies the
provider's missing-method action through the shared workspace-edit owner.
The returned transaction contains **only the probe buffer**; its text has the
new `private static String missingMessage()` declaration. Shared definition
navigation maps the call back to that declaration.

The fixture subscribes to the existing Buffer diagnostic event. Both repair and
restoration require a later diagnostic update with no errors, so an unchanged
empty diagnostic snapshot cannot satisfy recovery. This is bounded current-buffer
workflow evidence. It does not certify document-version correlation or rejection
of arbitrarily delayed unversioned diagnostics; the provider's earlier missing
versions remain an open stale-diagnostic limit. No diagnostic, edit, completion,
result or lifecycle owner is added or changed in production code.

## Active Java Debug trust revocation in the combined workflow — 2026-10-02

Task **6.1** now verifies trust revocation while an actual Java main is paused,
in the same cached Project as provider import, Editor edits, Dependencies,
build and selected Tests. The existing **debugger_tools::LogStore** observes
RPC through its existing DAP lifecycle subscription. Both launches require an
actual `stopped` event with reason `breakpoint`, Java Debug's custom
`processid` event with `processId`, and a positive host PID existence check.
The private observer keeps this Java-specific interpretation out of shared
DAP models. No protocol messages are injected and no new log/result store is
created.

The first launch hits the current Editor breakpoint at **Main.java:5**, selects
that source frame, and toolbar Continue must terminate its session and actual
process. A distinct second session resolves a fresh current Java Debug TCP
endpoint and remains paused at the same source breakpoint. The test-only
callback returns only its existing Session handle and actual PID to the
shared fixture's trust teardown. Restriction must terminate that paused
Session and PID, clear the active source position, clear Dependencies
navigation and stop both real JVM provider PIDs. Provider/JDTLS/Kotlin state,
Editor, Tasks/TerminalPanel, Tests/structured results, Debug UI/DapStore/Session
and trust ownership remain unchanged.

Both complete macOS ARM64 journeys pass: **45.82 seconds normally** and
**41.43 seconds with external network denied**, one test each. These timings
are separate cached samples, not a performance comparison with earlier runs.
Explicit cache/JDK prerequisites, the pinned Java Debug/JDTLS/official Kotlin
inputs, existing IPv4 loopback setting and the standalone probe's denial
boundary remain as before. The current shared suite passes **24 Tasks/Tests**
with 10 opt-in cases ignored (17.36s), **59 Debug UI** with this case ignored
(13.66s), and **4 DAP tests**. Warning-denied owner Clippy, Rust/docs formatting,
Copper graphs and both canonical validators pass with the recorded manual
ownership/decomposition audit. Existing validator breadth/overlap and
linker/future-compatibility warnings remain qualified. The full `docs/src`
format check also reports existing issues in `installation.md`,
`languages/csharp.md` and `migrate/vs-code.md`; both changed Groovy pages
pass the targeted format check.

The ledger retains missing constructor-trait and constructor-callback compile
errors, plus the first PID-observer failure. That observer incorrectly assumed
the standard `process`/`systemProcessId` shape. The correction uses the custom
Java Debug event already handled by the existing pinned standalone probe;
the actual-PID oracle and breakpoint-reason requirement stay intact. No
production transport, trust, log, result, provider or catalog code changed.
The setup guide now distinguishes this CLI evidence from physical and
installed-default journeys.

## Kotlin owned-process resource samples and daemon exit correction — 2026-10-02

Task **1.5** adds optional `--sample-process-resources` to the existing
standalone Kotlin probe. `/bin/ps` supplies only numeric PID, parent, process
group and RSS fields; command lines and unrelated application content are
never collected. Each sample follows the probe’s server group/current
descendants and daemons recorded in its fresh isolated Gradle 8.13 registry.
Combined samples union those sets before summing RSS. Independent maxima
can overlap and must not be added together. The opt-in option leaves ordinary
product startup and normal unsampled probes unchanged.

A real owned-process control uncovered an existing shutdown-evidence bug:
`Path.stem` turns `daemon-<pid>.out.log` into `daemon-<pid>.out`, so numeric
filtering could leave the prior exit loop with no PIDs. That earlier loop alone
cannot prove daemon termination. The corrected helper strips the full suffix
and rejects malformed/nonpositive IDs. Both resource aggregation and the
existing isolated `--stop` liveness loop now use it. Historical semantic and
import results retain their scope; the current runs supply the corrected
actual-PID shutdown evidence. The initial failed control/source are retained.

`python3 script/test-groovy-kotlin-resources.py` now creates an owned parent,
child and separately grouped daemon, plus a larger unrelated process. It
requires exactly those three owned processes, daemon inclusion, unrelated
process exclusion, explicit denied-inventory failure and malformed registry
rejection, then terminates only its own process groups. This control passes.
It is a bounded validation fixture, with no shared platform service, provider
SDK, result store or duplicate UI framework. Copper and existing product
owners are unchanged.

### Actual pinned candidate measurements

The host is **Apple M5, Mac17,2, 32 GiB RAM, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), ARM64**.
The existing publisher-checksummed official archive remains
`95da3fc6d3b9092c7616345044a05edb85e5408dc648d081e4e433595c892bec`.
All **773 regular files and 221 symlinks** in that archive match the installed
SDK used here; the manifest records individual hashes. This verifies these
inputs, without resolving standalone SDK distribution terms or a package gate.
The candidate reports **ILS-263.4702.0**. The explicit import build JDK is
**21.0.12.1+1-LTS**; current exported compatibility is `JDK_21`, which is not
a product Tasks/test runtime contract. This official candidate reused its
verified local archive; no official server was downloaded or distributed.

With 500 added Kotlin sources and independent cloned caches/daemon registries,
both external-network-denied Gradle launches pass import, `GroovyScale499.kt`
symbols, `Greeting.kt` definition, `message` completion, invalid-edit diagnostic
and clean restoration, and export of seven modules/eleven libraries/one SDK.
Each actual daemon independently reports denied external TCP, loopback-only
listeners and verified PID exit after `--stop`.

**The alpha/resource gate remains open.** Sampled RSS sums can double-count

## Remote JVM spawn diagnostic privacy (2026-10-02)

Task 5.3 and requirement 6.4 own this correction on macOS ARM64, after
fast-forward integration of Copper’s Rust discovery privacy change
`18b5e2cbfe44f3e14ede1819abe14b981003693c`. The JVM lifecycle previously
truncated raw Task errors to 256 characters at both conversion boundaries;
that still exported private-looking paths and token-like text. The retained
wire-unit and connected host regression each run one test and fail before
correction. The initial mistaken module filter runs zero tests and receives
no validation credit.

The existing JVM provider now emits “The Java test Task failed to start;
inspect the Task terminal and project-host logs” and reduces older-peer
SpawnError text to the same message before the registered host handler applies
it to StructuredExecutionStore. The local Task handle retains its original
error. No raw error logging is added. Other lifecycle states, identities,
protocol version, grants, shared result filtering, Tests and terminal owners
remain unchanged; the correction adds no generic error framework, result store,
Cargo interpretation or panel owner.

The exact final sources pass:

| Check                                  | Result                                               | Limit                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

### Product choices proposed before the accepted answers

This historical proposal was unanswered when recorded. The actual human answers
are recorded in the accepted-decisions section below and supersede its pending
status; proposed options alone never constituted acceptance.

| Decision / existing owner                              | Concrete options                                                                                                                                                                                | Recommendation for review                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Agent result access / Groovy 5.3                       | Keep sharing unadvertised and the gate open; or implement a bounded internal reader through the existing store and permission owner, with module filtering and immediate held-result revocation | Keep it unadvertised for the focused first release; do not claim agent acceptance                          |
| Kotlin alpha reference and resources / Groovy 1.5      | Qualify macOS ARM64 on 32 GiB with a proposed 8 GiB combined resident ceiling; require a 16 GiB reference with a proposed 4 GiB ceiling; or keep experimental status until the budget is agreed | Start with the 32 GiB reference, subject to owner acceptance and measured complete-workflow qualification  |
| Provider delivery / Groovy 1.1                         | Extension-managed downloads; or prepare bundling after authoritative redistribution terms and complete notice/source delivery                                                                   | Extension-managed downloads, retaining provenance, immutable selection, notice/delivery and platform gates |
| Publisher identity/update hosting / flavor 7.2 and 7.4 | Supply publisher-owned reverse-DNS root, updater service and intended platform cells; or retain provisional development identity and leave packaging blocked                                    | Keep production packaging blocked until concrete identity and hosting are supplied                         |

The proposed resource ceilings are product choices rather than measured
results. Existing RSS samples exclude the editor, may double-count shared
pages and may miss brief/detached workers; they do not qualify either limit.
The accepted method must include the editor and every owned JVM/build worker
and retain its measurement limitations. No option clears provider legal terms,
notice delivery, screen-reader/platform checks or final flavor enablement.
